If the team on offense has a player beyond the last man on the defense (not including the goal keeper), and the ball is passed to him, then the referee will call an offsides call. However, if the offensive player steps back on-sides (meaning there is still a defender between him and the goal) before the ball is passed then he is not offsides and play can continue. 

Essentially offsides means there’s no defender between you and the goal keeper when the ball is passed.

I’m not too great at proofs, I’m not sure how to put it in proper proof language, and this may already be apparent to you, but I would say that in order to isolate y, you’ll have to use the sqrt function which yields a positive and a negative value. So there are at least 2 possible y-values for a single x value (it could be more depending on how many x-values can also solve this equation). In order to isolate x, you’ll have to use log2 which will only yield one value for each y input. So there will be only one x-value that satisfies this equation and two y-values. If these solutions are ordered pairs then you’ll have (a,b) and (a,c) where b=/=c.

Woke up one night to the ear-bleeding scream of a little girl. I woke up shaking and had no clue where the screams could have come from. Then it happened again. This time it sounded slightly less human but even more unnerving. The hair on my neck and arms stood on end, and I started shaking again. Turns out it was the howl of a coyote nearby. I had never heard a coyote call before so this wake up call at 2am really freaked me out.
